statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains low because CME equity index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress holds in the high band on a 5.18% 10-year yield near its highest since the financial crisis, WTI at $92.41 with the Strait of Hormuz still closed, a rejected Iranian reopening roadmap, and 19 vessels targeted in the strait across Friday and Saturday.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart into the early Asian hours, where the withdrawn diplomatic premise behind part of Friday's oil decline would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures shut, while a hardening Hormuz stance, weekend tanker strikes and a 5.18% 10-year yield hold Stress high into the 22:00Z restart
body: Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so there is no live NQ price path at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects an absent path rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% from a 30,478.90 prior close and inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87. The week to 25 September was a risk-positive one in which equities absorbed a bond sell-off, with the 10-year yield reaching 5.18% after touching 5.225% intraweek, the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47% on the latest H.15 release. Weekend evidence hardened rather than eased. Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days in exchange for lifting the naval blockade and oil sanctions was rejected, Tehran says it is awaiting a definitive response, a senior Iranian general tied any reopening to an end of what Iran calls US economic warfare, and Iranian forces targeted 19 vessels described as violators across Friday and Saturday. Part of Friday's 2.33% WTI decline to $92.41 rested on that now-rejected roadmap, which leaves a withdrawn premise to be expressed at the 22:00Z CME restart in the thinnest liquidity of the week. That is conditional gap and repricing risk, not observed mean-reversion failure, so Tail stays in the low band and Stress carries the elevated reading instead. Confidence is high but not higher because the live NQ price path is genuinely unavailable, the shared Finviz context was stale and partial at run time, and Brent quotes conflicted across sources. One risk was removed: the September 30 funding deadline no longer threatens a shutdown after Congress extended funding to December 11. The week ahead is heavy, with PCE and GDP on Wednesday and September payrolls on Friday.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were carried forward unchanged. Tail held in a narrow 6-8 band, Stress rose steadily from 53 to 69, and Confidence decayed from 80 to a 67 trough around 08:00Z before recovering to 78 as weekend evidence was verified. The mapped state remained EA_ON with dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a closed-futures weekend in which risk accumulated through headlines rather than through an observed price path.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours, so the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout. Risk holds near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday, then lifts into the published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart, where the rejected Hormuz roadmap and the weekend's tanker strikes meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. From the early Asian hours the path steps back down on the assumption that reopening imbalance is absorbed with visible retracements, and rises again modestly into Monday's 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed print, which are checkpoints rather than structural Tail drivers. Every elevated forecast hour is conditional gap or continuation risk; none asserts that one-way structure has already been observed. Stress stays high throughout on a 5.18% 10-year yield and an unresolved Hormuz closure, and Wednesday's PCE and Friday's payrolls dominate the wider week.
